input: Build a fire pit in the backyard this fall

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether this is an in-ground pit, an above-ground ring, or a built-up stone/brick structure completely changes the materials, labor, and steps involved.
Knowing if this is a solo DIY project or involves hired contractors or helpers determines how tasks are assigned and what skills are required.
The specific backyard conditions — size, terrain, soil type, and local regulations or HOA rules — affect placement, permitting, and design choices.
The budget sets a hard ceiling on materials and labor, distinguishing a simple $50 gravel ring from a $2,000+ masonry build.
Whether the user already has tools and materials or needs to source everything determines the very first concrete action to take.
Aesthetic preferences — rustic stone, modern steel, brick — drive material selection and the overall design direction.
Knowing the intended use (occasional family gatherings vs. frequent entertaining) sets the standard for size, seating capacity, and finish quality.

gold.taskTitle: Build a backyard fire pit this fall
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to construct a fire pit in their backyard during the fall season.

questions.title: What type of fire pit structure do you want to build?
questions.description: In-ground pit, above-ground stone/brick ring, metal bowl insert, or full masonry structure — the type defines the entire scope of work.

questions.title: Will you build it yourself or hire help?
questions.description: Determines whether the plan is a DIY step-by-step guide or a contractor-coordination checklist.

questions.title: Are there local permits or HOA rules you need to follow?
questions.description: Local codes, setback requirements, or neighborhood rules can dictate placement, size, and whether a burn permit is needed before any digging starts.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this project?
questions.description: Sets the hard financial ceiling that governs material quality, size, and whether professional labor is feasible.

questions.title: Do you already have tools and materials, or start from scratch?
questions.description: Knowing what is already on hand determines whether the first step is a shopping run, a tool rental, or jumping straight into site prep.

questions.title: What look or style do you want the fire pit to have?
questions.description: Rustic fieldstone, clean modern steel, classic brick, or reclaimed wood surround — aesthetic preference drives material choices and design plans.

questions.title: How many people do you plan to seat around it regularly?
questions.description: Intended group size drives the diameter of the pit and the scale of any surrounding seating area, defining what 'done well' looks like in use.
